title: Finite projective modules lift over an etale neighbourhood of a closed subscheme
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $\overline P$ a finite projective $A/I$-module (a direct summand of a finite free $A/I$-module). Then there are a ring map $A\to A'$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and the induced map $\alpha:A/I\to A'/IA'$ is an isomorphism, and a finite projective $A'$-module $P'$ together with an isomorphism of $A'/IA'$-modules $P'/IP'\cong\overline P\otimes_{A/I}A'/IA'$ (the tensor product formed via $\alpha$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07M5 (lemma-lift-projective-module, line 2020) and its proof (projector lifted to A^n, characteristic polynomial, idempotent of B/IB lifted by Lemma lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs)

proof.text: *A projector and its lift.* Since $\overline P$ is a direct summand of a finite free $A/I$-module, choose $n\ge0$, an $A/I$-module $\overline K$ and an isomorphism $\theta:\overline P\oplus\overline K\xrightarrow{\sim}(A/I)^{\oplus n}$. Let $\bar p=\theta\circ(\mathrm{id}_{\overline P}\oplus0)\circ\theta^{-1}$, an endomorphism of $(A/I)^{\oplus n}$ with $\bar p\circ\bar p=\bar p$ and $\operatorname{Im}(\bar p)=\theta(\overline P)\cong\overline P$; let $\overline X\in M_n(A/I)$ be its matrix in the standard basis. Since $A\to A/I$ is surjective, choose $X\in M_n(A)$ reducing entrywise to $\overline X$, and let $\varphi:A^{\oplus n}\to A^{\oplus n}$ be the $A$-linear map with matrix $X$ (a lift of $\bar p$).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5 (lemma-lift-projective-module), first two sentences ('choose an integer n and a direct sum decomposition (A/I)^n = P-bar (+) K-bar ... Choose a lift phi of the projector p-bar'; Stacks writes R/I for A/I there, a typo)

proof.text: *The ring $B$ and Cayley-Hamilton.* Let $f=\det(x-\varphi)\in A[x]$ be the characteristic polynomial of $\varphi$ [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module]; it is monic of degree $n$ [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties] (c). Put $B=A[x]/(f)$; it is a free $A$-module with basis the classes of $1,x,\dots,x^{n-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], hence a finite $A$-algebra and integral over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. By Cayley-Hamilton [lem-weil-cayley-hamilton-free-module], $f(\varphi)=0$ in $\operatorname{End}_A(A^{\oplus n})=M_n(A)$. The $A$-algebra map $A[x]\to M_n(A)$, $x\mapsto X$ (well defined since $A$ acts by central scalar matrices; its image is the commutative subring $A[X]$) kills $f$, so it factors through an $A$-algebra map $\psi:B\to M_n(A)$ with $\psi(x)=X$. Reducing entries modulo $I$ maps $\psi(IB)$ into $M_n(I)$, so $\psi$ induces an $A$-algebra map $\bar\psi:B/IB\to M_n(A/I)$ with $\bar\psi(\bar x)=\overline X$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5, third to fifth sentences ('Let f in A[x] be the characteristic polynomial of phi. Set B = A[x]/(f). By Cayley-Hamilton (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00DX, lemma-charpoly) there is a map B -> End_A(A^n) mapping x to phi'); integrality of B, used later without mention, written out by the agent

proof.text: *$x(1-x)$ is nilpotent modulo $IB$.* Let $\mathfrak Q\subset B$ be a prime with $IB\subseteq\mathfrak Q$ and $\mathfrak p\subset A$ its preimage, so $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. The map $A/\mathfrak p\to B/\mathfrak Q$ is injective, so it extends to a field embedding $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak Q)=\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak Q)$. Let $\lambda:A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the canonical map; it factors through $A/I$, so $\lambda(X)$ (entrywise) is the image of the idempotent matrix $\overline X$, hence idempotent. By [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties] (d) the characteristic polynomial of $\lambda(X)$ is $\lambda(f)$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-endomorphism-charpoly-field] $\lambda(f)=(x-1)^rx^{n-r}$ for some $r$, which divides $x^n(x-1)^n$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[x]$. Let $\xi\in\kappa(\mathfrak Q)$ be the image of $x$; the ring map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[x]\to\kappa(\mathfrak Q)$, $x\mapsto\xi$, sends $\lambda(f)$ to the image of $f(x)=0$, hence sends $x^n(x-1)^n$ to $0$: $\xi^n(\xi-1)^n=0$ in the field $\kappa(\mathfrak Q)$, so $\xi\in\{0,1\}$ and $\xi(1-\xi)=0$, i.e. $x(1-x)\in\mathfrak Q$. Thus $x(1-x)$ lies in every prime of $B$ containing $IB$, hence in $\sqrt{IB}$ [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq]: there is $N\ge1$ with $x^N(1-x)^N\in IB$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5, sixth to ninth sentences ('For every prime p containing I the image of f in kappa(p) is (x-1)^r x^{n-r} ... Hence x^N(1-x)^N is contained in IB for some N >= 1'); the passage from primes of A to primes of B/IB written out by the agent

proof.text: *The idempotent $\bar e$ of $B/IB$ and its image $\bar p$.* In $\overline B=B/IB$ put $s=\bar x^N$, $t=(1-\bar x)^N$; then $st=0$ (step 3). In $\mathbf Z[x]$, $1=(x+(1-x))^{2N-1}=\sum_i\binom{2N-1}{i}x^i(1-x)^{2N-1-i}$ and each term has $i\ge N$ or $2N-1-i\ge N$, so $1=a\,x^N+b\,(1-x)^N$ with $a,b\in\mathbf Z[x]$; hence $as+bt=1$ in $\overline B$. Then $s=s(as+bt)=as^2$, $t=bt^2$, and $(s+t)(a^2s+b^2t)=a(as^2)+b(bt^2)=as+bt=1$, so $s+t=\bar x^N+(1-\bar x)^N$ is a unit, and $\bar e:=s(s+t)^{-1}=a^2s^2=as$ satisfies $\bar e^2=a(as^2)=as=\bar e$: $\bar e=\bar x^N/(\bar x^N+(1-\bar x)^N)$ is an idempotent. Since $\bar\psi(\bar x)=\overline X$ is idempotent, $\bar\psi(s)=\overline X^N=\overline X$ and $\bar\psi(t)=(1-\overline X)^N=1-\overline X$, so $\bar\psi(s+t)=1$ and $\bar\psi(\bar e)=\overline X\cdot1=\overline X$ (inside the commutative subring $(A/I)[\overline X]$).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5, tenth to twelfth sentences ('It follows that x^N + (1-x)^N is a unit in B/IB and that e-bar = image of x^N/(x^N+(1-x)^N) is an idempotent as both assertions hold in Z[x]/(x^N(x-1)^N). The image of e-bar in End_{A/I}((A/I)^n) is ... = p-bar'); the explicit inverse written out by the agent

proof.text: *Lifting $\bar e$ over an etale neighbourhood.* Since $B$ is integral over $A$ (step 2) and $\bar e\in B/IB$ is idempotent (step 4), [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotent-upstairs] gives a ring map $\sigma:A\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $\alpha:A/I\to A'/IA'$ an isomorphism, and an idempotent $e'\in B\otimes_AA'$ with $\rho(e')=\bar e$, where $\rho$ is the composite $B\otimes_AA'\to B\otimes_A(A'/IA')\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\alpha^{-1}}B\otimes_A(A/I)=B/IB$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5, thirteenth sentence ('After replacing A by an etale extension A' as in the lemma, we may assume there exists an idempotent e in B which maps to e-bar in B/IB, see Lemma Tag 07M4')

proof.text: *The idempotent matrix $p$ over $A'$ lifts $\bar p$.* Let $\sigma(\psi(b))\in M_n(A')$ denote entrywise application of $\sigma$. The map $B\times A'\to M_n(A')$, $(b,a')\mapsto a'\,\sigma(\psi(b))$, is $A$-bilinear, so it induces an additive map $\psi':B\otimes_AA'\to M_n(A')$; it is multiplicative because scalar matrices are central and $\sigma(\psi(B))$ is commutative, so $\psi'$ is a ring map. Put $p=\psi'(e')$, an idempotent of $M_n(A')$. Let $\pi':M_n(A')\to M_n(A'/IA')$ and $\bar\alpha:M_n(A/I)\to M_n(A'/IA')$ be the entrywise maps. The two ring maps $\pi'\circ\psi'$ and $\bar\alpha\circ\bar\psi\circ\rho$ from $B\otimes_AA'$ to $M_n(A'/IA')$ agree on $b\otimes1$ (both give the entrywise image of $\psi(b)$ under $A\to A/I\xrightarrow{\alpha}A'/IA'$, which equals $A\xrightarrow{\sigma}A'\to A'/IA'$) and on $1\otimes a'$ (both give the scalar matrix of $a'\bmod IA'$, as $\rho(1\otimes a')=\alpha^{-1}(a'\bmod IA')\cdot1$); since these elements generate $B\otimes_AA'$ as a ring, the maps are equal. Hence $\pi'(p)=\bar\alpha(\bar\psi(\rho(e')))=\bar\alpha(\bar\psi(\bar e))=\bar\alpha(\overline X)$ by step 4.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5, last two sentences ('Then the image of e under the map B = A[x]/(f) -> End_A(A^n) is an idempotent element p which lifts p-bar'); the compatibility of the maps after the base change to A' written out by the agent

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Let $P'=\operatorname{Im}(p)\subseteq A'^{\oplus n}$, $p$ viewed as an endomorphism of $A'^{\oplus n}$; by [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-endomorphism-image-base-change] (i) it is a finite projective $A'$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-endomorphism-image-base-change] (ii) for $R=A'$, $S=A'/IA'$ and the idempotent $p$ (step 6): $P'/IP'=P'\otimes_{A'}A'/IA'\cong\operatorname{Im}(\pi'(p))=\operatorname{Im}(\bar\alpha(\overline X))$ as $A'/IA'$-modules. By the same lemma (ii) for $R=A/I$, $S=A'/IA'$ via $\alpha$ and the idempotent $\bar p$ (matrix $\overline X$): $\overline P\otimes_{A/I}A'/IA'\cong\operatorname{Im}(\bar p)\otimes_{A/I}A'/IA'\cong\operatorname{Im}(\bar\alpha(\overline X))$ (step 1). Composing, $P'/IP'\cong\overline P\otimes_{A/I}A'/IA'$ as $A'/IA'$-modules. Together with step 5 ($\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale, $\alpha$ an isomorphism) this proves the lemma.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5, last sentence ('Setting P = Im(p) we win'); the meaning of 'lifting' (P'/IP' = P-bar via alpha) checked by the agent

Proof written in 7 steps following the Stacks proof: projector and lift, B = A[x]/(f) with f the characteristic polynomial and the Cayley-Hamilton map, x(1-x) nilpotent mod IB via the fibres, the idempotent x^N/(x^N+(1-x)^N) with explicit inverse, lift by 07M4 (existing node lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotent-upstairs), compatibility of the lifted idempotent matrix with p-bar, and P' = Im(p). Existing nodes cited: charpoly definition and properties, monic-quotient-free, finite-algebra-is-integral, Cayley-Hamilton (sec-zeta-weil Mathlib leaf, a tool), zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq. Two new unsplit nodes: the characteristic polynomial of an idempotent over a field (stated without proof in Stacks) and the image of an idempotent endomorphism of a finite free module (finite projective, commutes with base change).

lean.statement: theorem lift_finite_projective_module_etale (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (Pbar : Type v) [AddCommGroup Pbar] [Module (A ⧸ I) Pbar] [Module.Finite (A ⧸ I) Pbar] [Module.Projective (A ⧸ I) Pbar] : ∃ (A' : CommRingCat.{u}) (g : CommRingCat.of A ⟶ A'), letI : Algebra A A' := g.hom.toAlgebra; Etale (Spec.map g) ∧ ∃ α : A ⧸ I ≃+* A' ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A A'), (∀ a : A, α (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap A A' a)) ∧ ∃ (P' : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup P') (_ : Module A' P'), Module.Finite A' P' ∧ Module.Projective A' P' ∧ letI : Algebra (A ⧸ I) (A' ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A A')) := α.toRingHom.toAlgebra; Nonempty ((P' ⧸ (I.map (algebraMap A A') • (⊤ : Submodule A' P'))) ≃ₗ[ A' ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A A')] ((A' ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A A')) ⊗[A ⧸ I] Pbar))
